question: How many of its own shares did Apple buy back in 2026, and for how much?
answer: Apple repurchased roughly 297 million of its own shares in 2026, spending about $85.8 billion on those buybacks. The 2026 Form 10‑K reports a repurchase of 297 million shares for $85.8 billion [1] and confirms the $85.8 billion repurchase amount for the year [2].

Recent Accounting Pronouncements

Internal-Use Software

In September 2025, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (“FASB”) issued Accounting Standards Update (“ASU”) No. 2025-06, Intangibles—Goodwill and Other—Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software (“ASU 2025-06”), which modernizes the accounting for internal-use software. ASU 2025-06 removes all references to software development stages and requires capitalization of software costs when management has committed to the software project and it is probable the software will be completed and perform its intended use. ASU 2025-06 will be effective for the Company in its first quarter of 2029, and early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the timing and method of its adoption of ASU 2025-06.

retrieved.section: Item 7 — Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
retrieved.text:
The Company also issues unsecured short-term promissory notes pursuant to a commercial paper program. As of September 26, 2026, the Company had $2.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding, which was payable within 12 months.

Leases

The Company has lease arrangements for certain equipment and facilities, including corporate, data center, manufacturing and retail space. As of September 26, 2026, the Company had fixed lease payment obligations of $17.8 billion, with $2.8 billion payable within 12 months.

Manufacturing Purchase Obligations

The Company utilizes several outsourcing partners to manufacture subassemblies for the Company’s products and to perform final assembly and testing of finished products. The Company also obtains individual components for its products from a wide variety of individual suppliers. As of September 26, 2026, the Company had manufacturing purchase obligations of $89.7 billion, with $82.7 billion payable within 12 months.

Other Purchase Obligations

The Company’s other purchase obligations primarily consist of noncancelable obligations related to supplier arrangements, licensed content and intellectual property, distribution rights, and the acquisition of capital assets. As of September 26, 2026, the Company had other purchase obligations of $27.3 billion, with $9.9 billion payable within 12 months.

Capital Return Program

In addition to its contractual cash requirements, the Company has authorized share repurchase programs. The programs do not obligate the Company to acquire a minimum amount of shares. As of September 26, 2026, the Company’s quarterly cash dividend was $0.27 per share. The Company intends to increase its dividend on an annual basis, subject to declaration by the Board.

In April 2026, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.26 to $0.27 per share beginning in May 2026.

As of September 26, 2026, remaining availability under the May 2025 program was $14.0 billion. On April 30, 2026, the Company announced an additional program to repurchase up to $100 billion of the Company’s common stock. The programs do not obligate the Company to acquire a minimum amount of shares. Under the programs, shares may be repurchased in privately negotiated or open market transactions, including under plans complying with Rule 10b5-1 under the Exchange Act.

(2)In May 2026, the Company entered into accelerated share repurchase agreements (“ASRs”). Under the terms of the ASRs, financial institutions committed to deliver shares of the Company’s common stock during the purchase periods in exchange for up-front payments totaling $10.0 billion. In August 2026, the purchase periods for the ASRs ended and 6 million shares were delivered and retired. In total, 33 million shares were delivered under the ASRs at an average repurchase price of $305.29 per share.
